title: Magnific AI MCP: Image Upscaling and Enhancement Guide
summary: Magnific AI MCP enables direct integration of image upscaling tools into your development environment. You can automate high-resolution workflows.
body_markdown:
## Step 1: Install the Magnific MCP server locally


Integrating Magnific into a local environment requires establishing a secure bridge between the Magnific API and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) host.


This setup transitions the tool from a manual web interface to a background service that high-reasoning models, such as Claude Sonnet 5.5, can call to execute image enhancements.


### Generate your Magnific API credentials


Accessing the Magnific engine programmatically requires a unique API key to authenticate requests and bill usage to the correct account. Without this credential, the MCP server can't authorize the external processing of high-resolution image data.


You must navigate to the Magnific User Dashboard, locate the API Settings tab, and generate a new secret token. This key acts as a sensitive administrative password; exposing it in public version control allows unauthorized third parties to consume your processing credits.


### Download and install the Magnific MCP server


The Magnific MCP server is distributed as a Node.js package that you can install directly from the official repository or via the Node Package Manager. You must have Node.js installed on your machine to execute the server as a background process for your AI agent.


To install the server, add` https://mcp.magnific.com` as a streamable HTTP MCP server in your client — no local installation is required. This command downloads the latest stable build and places the executable in your global path, making it accessible to Claude Desktop.


### Configure Claude Desktop to use Magnific MCP


Claude Desktop relies on a specific configuration file to identify and launch local MCP servers during startup. By modifying this JSON file, you instruct your AI agent to recognize the Magnific server as an available capability.


The configuration file is located at` ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` on macOS and` %APPDATA%\\Claude\\claude_desktop_config.json` on Windows. You must ensure the directory exists before attempting to save your edits.


The following JSON structure registers the Magnific server within the` mcpServers` object. You must replace the placeholder with your actual secret token to enable the connection.


```text
{
"mcpServers": {
"magnific": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["-y", "@magnific-ai/mcp-server"],
"env": {
"MAGNIFIC_API_KEY": "your_api_key_here"
}
}
}
}
```


Successful execution of these steps ensures your agent loads the necessary environment variables, including the` MAGNIFIC_API_KEY` , which is required for the server to communicate with the enhancement engine.


### Verify the Magnific MCP server connection


Confirming the installation ensures that your agent can successfully handshake with the server before you attempt complex automation workflows. In the Claude Desktop interface, a hammer icon or "Tools" menu will display the active Magnific functions if your configuration is valid.


If the tools don't appear, the application logs will typically show a file path error, indicating your agent can't find the server executable. Once verified, your agent gains the ability to autonomously upscale images, allowing it to handle visual refinement tasks without manual file uploads.
